content.title: Can you see the Artemis II splash down off the California coast?
content.text: California ranks fourth-highest in the nation for child-rearing expenses. SAN DIEGO — A new LendingTree report reveals the dramatic cost of raising a child in California, with expenses now totaling more than $312,300 through age 18—an 8.8% increase from last year's $286,951. The annual lending marketplace report examined factors including rent, food and childcare costs across all 50 states. California ranks fourth-highest in the nation for child-rearing expenses, trailing only Massachusetts, Maryland and Hawaii, which tops the list at more than $412,000. The high costs present a challenge for families statewide. "That's an incredibly daunting number… and unfortunately, it doesn't seem like it's getting a whole lot better anytime soon," said Matt Schulz, LendingTree's Chief Consumer Finance Analyst. Expensive daycare drives much of California's burden, particularly during a child's first five years. "What we found was in California — especially in those first five years of life — when you factor in daycare costs, it had one of the highest costs for raising a child in the entire country, in part because daycare is so expensive nationally," Schulz said. Financial experts and parents offer practical strategies to manage mounting expenses. Schulz recommends that prospective parents begin saving early to build a financial cushion. "The more money you can put away into a high-yield savings account and let it grow, the greater buffer you'll have when you take on these costs," Schulz said. For current parents experiencing financial strain, strategic lifestyle adjustments can free up resources. Schulz suggests considering relocation to more affordable areas. "As much as you may want that apartment a few blocks from the beach in San Diego, it may not fit your lifestyle anymore — or your pocketbook. It may make sense to move further inland to free up money for the extra costs of raising a kid," Schulz said. A San Diego mother of two has built a following by sharing cost-saving strategies. Yesenia Auer operates the popular Instagram account San Diego Girl Mom, which boasts more than 41,000 followers and emphasizes that families need not spend money to create meaningful experiences. "There's a big misconception that you have to spend money to have a good time or create those memories with your kids. But if you focus on what you can do versus what you can't, it opens up a big world of possibilities," said Auer. Libraries offer numerous free resources that many families overlook, according to Auer. "The library — that's a good one. There are summer reading programs, and you get free passes to museums. You can also go on the library's website and download passes to the zoo, the Children's Museum… there are so many passes on there, but people don't know about them," she said. Community organizations stand ready to assist families seeking financial relief. "There are places out there willing and eager to help you. You just need to seek those things out, because they can make a real difference," said Auer.
